items.stem: When the air above a lake stays below freezing for several days, its surface water loses heat and a layer of ice forms. On most lakes in the region, Lake Orven among them, this ice is thin and melts every spring. Lake Talva is different: it lies in the shadow of a steep cliff that blocks most of the sunlight, and its ice therefore stays thick all year. According to the paragraph, which of the following statements about Lake Orven is not correct?
options: It gets less sunlight than Lake Talva
Its ice is thin compared with Lake Talva's
The air above it can stay below freezing
Its ice does not remain throughout the year
items.explanation: Lake Talva's thick ice is explained by the cliff that blocks its sunlight, so Lake Orven, with thin ice, cannot be the one that gets less sunlight. (2) and (4) follow from the contrast between the lakes, and (3) is true because ice forms on Lake Orven.

items.stem: Scholars disagree over what the art theorist Aurel Menck saw as the calling of the painter. One group maintains that although Menck writes in his treatise that the goal of painting is the perfect imitation of nature, he cannot have regarded this as the painter's calling, because in the same treatise he argues that such imitation is beyond any painter's reach, since pigments can never reproduce the brightness of natural light. According to another group, Menck held that, even so, the painter's calling is to come as close to this goal as possible. Which of the following statements is correct according to the paragraph?
options: The scholars disagree about the goal Menck assigned to painting, since his treatise does not say what it is
The two groups differ over what, according to Menck, a perfect imitation of nature would consist of
Both groups of scholars agree that, according to Menck, no painter can fully achieve a perfect imitation of nature
The scholars disagree over whether, according to Menck, a painter's materials can make it possible to reach this goal
items.explanation: Both groups accept that, for Menck, perfect imitation is out of reach; they disagree only about the painter's calling. (1) is wrong because the treatise does state the goal, (2) raises a question nobody discusses, and (4) invents a disagreement on a point both groups agree on.

items.stem: A survey of a peat bog on the island of Harrow Tor has uncovered dozens of bone fishhooks, about 9,000 years old, all carved in one of only four standard sizes. According to the survey report, this uniformity shows that the island's early fishing people were already catching far more fish than they themselves needed - a practice that until now had been recorded on the island only among the farmers who settled there some 1,500 years later. Which of the following is not implied in the paragraph?
options: The peat bog on Harrow Tor preserved objects made of bone for thousands of years
The survey report treats the uniform size of the fishhooks as evidence of how much fish was caught
Farmers had already settled on Harrow Tor by the time the fishhooks found in the bog were carved
The farmers who later settled on Harrow Tor caught more fish than they themselves needed
items.explanation: The farmers settled on the island some 1,500 years after the hooks were made; the report says only that the earlier fishing people shared a practice known from the farmers, not that farmers were already there. (1), (2) and (4) all follow from the paragraph.

items.stem: Dr. Meital Sharon is known as "the defender of nurses." She says that those who claim human error is behind most mistakes in hospital wards are right, but only if "human error" is properly understood: "The administrator who plans the shifts, the engineer who designs the medicine labels, the pharmacist who prepares the doses, the lecturer who trained the staff – all of them are human, and nearly every mistake on a ward can be traced to an oversight by one of them. The nurse at the bedside is the one who must deal with everyone else's oversights." Why is Dr. Sharon known as "the defender of nurses"?
options: Because she maintains that although most mistakes on wards are due to human error, a considerable share of them are caused by faulty equipment
Because she believes that people who are not directly involved in treating the patient often bear part of the blame for mistakes
Because she argues that nurses, being human, cannot be expected never to make an error or overlook anything
Because she maintains that nurses often prevent harm to patients by successfully catching the oversights of other staff members
items.explanation: She widens "human error" to include people far from the bedside, so part of the blame shifts away from the nurse. (1) brings in non-human causes she never mentions, (3) excuses nurses on grounds she does not use, and (4) turns "has to deal with" into a claim that nurses succeed.

items.stem: Dr. Ronen: "A folk game that is passed down through generations rarely stays as it was. Rather than spreading in a single fixed form, it branches out: players in one town add a rule here, players in another change the scoring there, until each place has a version that is recognizably its own. It is precisely these local versions that give a town's residents a sense of shared identity and set them apart from the residents of neighboring towns." Which of the following processes best illustrates Dr. Ronen's claim?
options: A national sports association succeeded in making a traditional ball game popular throughout the country, although in the past it had been played in only a few remote villages
Although a certain card game was once played according to several different sets of rules, today players everywhere follow a single, uniform set of rules
The custom of holding a kite-flying contest on the first day of spring, which was once common in many towns, has almost completely disappeared
Today each town in the valley plays the stone-throwing game with its own detailed scoring rules, whereas at first the game had no fixed rules at all
items.explanation: A game with no fixed rules that branched into a detailed version for each town is exactly the process described. (1) is the spread of a game, (2) is the reverse process (many versions become one), and (3) is the decline of a custom.

items.stem: Artificial organs, such as mechanical hearts and implanted kidney devices, are judged by physicians not in relation to the devices that came before them but in relation to the living organ, which remains the model they are meant to match. This sets them apart from inventions in many other fields, whose novelty was expressed in the name they were given when they first appeared: the radio, for example, was at first known as "the wireless telegraph." Which of the following examples could best replace the example at the end of the paragraph?
options: Calling the electric refrigerator "an icebox without ice"
Calling a mechanical calculator "a clerk without a pencil"
Calling a submarine "an iron fish"
Calling a wind-up watch "a watch without a battery"
items.explanation: Like the wireless telegraph, the refrigerator is named after the earlier device it replaced, minus the element that defined that device. (2) and (3) measure the machine against a living model (a person, a fish), which is the contrast the paragraph draws, and a fish is not an earlier device that the submarine replaced; (4) names the older device after a feature of the newer one.

items.stem: A hotel wanted to stop guests from staying in their rooms past the official check-out time of noon, so the manager announced that guests would be charged a fee for every hour they stayed beyond noon. To the manager's surprise, the number of guests who checked out late rose sharply: many guests, it turned out, were glad to keep their rooms longer, as long as they could pay for it. Which of the following cases is most similar to the case described?
options: A baker saw that demand for his whole-wheat bread had grown, so he raised its price; to his surprise, he went on selling just as many loaves as before

A magazine stopped including its free travel booklet, and a separate travel magazine began to be sold at almost the same price as the original magazine; to the publisher's surprise, many readers stopped buying the original magazine and bought the travel magazine instead

A city's museums used to let visitors who arrived without booking a time slot enter anyway if there was room; to reduce such visits, the city began charging these visitors a high surcharge; to its surprise, the number of visitors arriving without a booking rose
After a long dispute, a company's management agreed to give its employees an extra day off every month; to its surprise, both output and profits grew
items.explanation: As at the hotel, a charge meant to deter a tolerated lapse turned it into a service people were willing to buy, and the lapse grew. (1) is a price rise that did not cut demand, (2) is readers switching to a new product, and (4) is a benefit that paid off.

items.stem: Noga: "I have noticed that whenever Eitan's grades fall, his private tutor has stopped coming to see him. Evidently she loses patience with him when he stops making an effort, and so she gives up on him each time his grades drop." Tami: "Your reasoning is about as sound as the claim that opening umbrellas is what makes it rain." What does Tami mean?
options: Had Eitan's tutor kept coming, his grades would have fallen even further
Eitan lets his grades fall because he wants his tutor to stop coming
Eitan's grades fall because his tutor stops coming to see him
Eitan's tutor is wrong to give up on him just when he needs her most
items.explanation: Umbrellas open because it rains, not the other way round: Tami says Noga has reversed cause and effect. (1) adds a "what if", (2) adds a motive, and (4) adds a moral judgment.

items.stem: Ofer, raising his voice so loudly that the whole office could hear him: "Dana, I was told that you shouted at the new intern this morning! I can hardly believe it. Surely you know that shouting at people never gets anything done." Dana: "If you stop for a moment and listen to yourself, you will see that it is like ____." Which of the following best completes Dana's words?
options: refusing to lend your neighbor a ladder only because he once refused to lend you his
writing a long, rambling letter to a newspaper to complain that people no longer express themselves briefly
going out to water your garden in the middle of a heavy rainstorm so that the plants will not dry out
complaining that a pickpocket took advantage of the fact that you left your wallet sticking out of your pocket
items.explanation: Ofer shouts in order to say that shouting is wrong, so his act undermines his own message, like a rambling letter demanding brevity. (1) is retaliation, (3) is a pointless act, and (4) shifts the blame for one's own carelessness.

items.stem: In a conversation between Maya and Itai, Maya made a remark, and Itai responded: "You sound like someone who decides how good a restaurant's food is by looking at the shape of its plates." Which of the following is most likely to be what Maya said?
options: "I tried on several pairs of running shoes and bought the most comfortable pair, even though it was expensive."
"The acting in Varden's new play is so wooden that I left at the intermission."
"The coffee at the corner café is too bitter for me – I won't go back there."
"Attorney Amir must be an outstanding lawyer – his office is in the most luxurious tower in the city."
items.explanation: Itai says Maya judges the main thing by an incidental detail, as in judging a lawyer by his office building. (1), (2) and (3) each judge the thing itself: comfort, acting, taste.

items.stem: Lior told Boaz that he had ordered a rare cookbook from a shop overseas and would have to wait two months for it to arrive. Boaz replied: "What you are doing is like swimming across a river while there is a bridge just a few steps away. The city library has had a copy of that very book on its shelves for years." In his reply, Boaz compares -
options: the copy in the city library to the bridge
ordering the book from overseas to the river
the cookbook to the bridge
the copy ordered from overseas to swimming across the river
items.explanation: The bridge is the easy way to the same place: the library copy. Ordering from overseas is the swimming, not the river (2); the book is what lies on the other side, not the bridge (3); the ordered copy is the goal, not the effort of getting there (4).

items.stem: Adi, who owns a bookshop, had its lighting replaced with bright white lamps in the hope of attracting more customers. Three weeks later she was disappointed to find that sales had declined, and she attributed the decline to the new lighting. Which of the following facts would support Adi's explanation?
options: Adi's bookshop specializes in rare books that are hard to find anywhere else in the city
The pharmacy across the street from Adi's shop is lit by bright white lamps and is always crowded
Ten days before Adi had the lamps replaced, a large bookstore offering steep discounts opened on the same street
In Adi's two other bookshops, where the lighting was not replaced, sales did not change during the same period
items.explanation: Shops without the new lighting saw no change, so the lighting is what set the declining shop apart. (1) is irrelevant, (2) is a counterexample, and (3) offers another cause of the decline.

items.stem: Ruth saw her neighbor, Mr. Adler, leave several wooden chairs painted bright yellow on the sidewalk for the garbage collectors. She concluded that Mr. Adler does not like yellow furniture. Which of the following statements does not weaken Ruth's conclusion?
options: Every piece of furniture in Mr. Adler's apartment is painted yellow
The chairs Mr. Adler put out had cracked or wobbly legs
Mr. Adler received the yellow chairs as a gift a month before his wedding
Mr. Adler's daughter had recently bought him a new dining set
items.explanation: When and how he got the chairs says nothing about why he threw them out. (1), (2) and (4) each give a reason other than dislike of yellow.

items.stem: In an experiment, Dr. Elkin formed two teams of volunteers – a team of three and a team of nine – and gave each team one hour to find, working together, as many as possible of the small objects hidden in a garden; each team searched a different garden of the same size. The team of nine found far more objects than the team of three, and Dr. Elkin hypothesized that the number of members in a team affects its success at this type of task. Which of the following statements strengthens Dr. Elkin's hypothesis?
options: One of the members of the team of nine had helped hide the objects before the experiment and remembered where several of them were
The members of the team of three had often taken part in such searches, whereas the members of the team of nine had never done so
Six of the members of the team of nine were called away before their team had begun searching the garden
The garden searched by the team of three was far more densely overgrown than the garden searched by the team of nine
items.explanation: The larger team won even though experience was on the smaller team's side, which rules out experience as the explanation. (1) and (4) give rival explanations, and (3) means the teams were really the same size.

items.stem: Given: The proportion of people with dry skin among those who use the cream Dermalin is higher than the proportion among the general population. Hypothesis: Dry skin is a side effect of using Dermalin. Which of the following findings weakens the hypothesis?
options: People who use an alternative cream to Dermalin do not suffer from dry skin
Dermatologists may recommend Dermalin only to people who do not have dry skin
Dermalin is a cream for relieving the itching caused by dry skin
One of the common side effects of Dermalin is a mild rash
items.explanation: If Dermalin is used because of dry skin, the dry skin comes first and the cream follows: cause and effect are reversed. (2) supports the hypothesis, and (1) and (4) do not bear on it.

items.stem: At dinner Noam ate a very spicy curry, and soon afterwards his mouth began to burn. Twenty minutes later he ate a portion of the dessert "Kolara," and the burning stopped. Noam concluded from this that vanilla, one of the ingredients of "Kolara," neutralizes the effect of hot spices. Which of the following does not weaken Noam's conclusion?
options: Noam drinks vanilla-flavored coffee almost every day, and it has never caused a burning sensation in his mouth
"Kolara" is made with a large amount of cream, and dairy products are known to ease the burning caused by hot spices
According to the chef, the burning caused by the spices in the curry Noam ate usually fades by itself within about ten minutes
The curry Noam ate contained hardly any hot spices, but it was seasoned with an herb to which Noam is sensitive, and his sensitivity shows itself as a burning sensation in the mouth
items.explanation: That vanilla does not cause burning says nothing about whether it relieves burning caused by spices. (2) offers another active ingredient, (3) the passage of time, and (4) another cause of the burning.

items.stem: At a certain youth soccer club, players who miss a practice without notice are recorded by the club secretary and are also given a penalty: at the next practice they must help the equipment manager collect and wash the balls. Last month the equipment manager was on leave, and the number of unexcused absences recorded was much lower than usual. The club director concluded that helping the equipment manager does not deter players from missing practice, since they enjoy his company. Which of the following facts may weaken the director's conclusion?
options: Two months ago a record was set both in the number of unexcused absences and in the number of players sent to help the equipment manager
At the start of last month the club announced that the team with the fewest unexcused absences this season would travel to a tournament abroad
When the equipment manager returned from leave, the number of unexcused absences went up again
Last month the players' school exam period began, which makes it harder for them to find time for practice
items.explanation: A prize announced at the same time offers another reason for the drop in absences. (3) supports the director, (4) should have raised absences, so the drop despite it also supports the conclusion, and (1) says nothing about last month.
